mentions.name: Loa
mentions.description: This app is an open source coding agent named Loa designed to run against self-hosted LLM environments such as Ollama, targeting non-cloud-sized models (e.g. a 27b model). It decomposes tasks into very simple single steps that smaller models can solve, dynamically mutates and restructures its execution plan as new context arrives, and maintains a layered memory/context system combining chat history, step results, an action backlog, reasoning explanations, and a working memory of facts and decisions. It provides a full observability UI showing memory contents, composed context, plan dependencies, artifacts, and an audit log of all executed actions, accepts mid-execution steering messages that can alter or mutate the plan, and includes error-correction and self-reflection logic (e.g. JSON repair fallbacks and hypothesis-driven retries or plan changes). It deliberately trades execution time (many inferences) for reasoning and result quality, aiming to be a hands-off agent that is briefed once and completes the task without constant reprompting, and can also serve as an analysis and discussion partner. A stable beta is planned for release.
mentions.problem: Existing coding agents target cloud-sized models and try to solve whole tasks in a handful of inferences, overloading the model and often requiring users to reprompt repeatedly until something is correctly solved; smaller self-hosted models struggle with monolithic multi-step tasks.
mentions.audience: Developers who want a hands-off coding agent running on self-hosted models
